subject: Renewal: FastRetail SLA upgrade & capacity term transition
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: FastRetail SLA upgrade & capacity term transition

Hi Anna —

Per our renewal window next month, quick summary proposal to align on:

- Term: 12 months (renewal effective 2027-03-01)
- Support tier: move from Standard -> Premium SLA (24/7 incident support with phone escalation, 30-minute response for Sev-1)
- Latency SLO: Premium SLA to include p95 inference latency target of <= 200ms for the agreed model family on provisioned capacity; fallback SLO for burst traffic clarified below
- Capacity: baseline commit to 250 dedicated GPU-hours/month with a 30% burst buffer for seasonal peaks (auto-billing at committed + usage tiers)
- Commercials: ~18% uplift on current ARR for the premium bundle (detailed line items attached)

Attachments: FastRetail_Renewal_MAAP_v2.pdf (order + pricing), SLA-Amendment-Redline.docx (internal draft)

Key asks from your side we want to confirm:
- Does the 30% burst window for Q3 suffice for your peak?
- Any procurement constraints on contract language (term, auto-renew, liability caps)?

If that looks reasonable I can circulate a redline to procurement and drop a DocuSign envelope for the amendment. Marissa — flagging for SRE/ops details and for Rishi if we need executive approval on the exception to the standard latency guarantees.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@fastretail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Wei Zhang <wei.zhang@fastretail.com>, FastRetail Procurement <procurement@fastretail.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: FastRetail SLA upgrade & capacity term transition

Sean — thanks for the clear summary. A few follow-ups from our end before we move to legal: 

1) Latency SLO specifics: can you confirm whether the p95 <= 200ms is measured at the model invocation boundary (post-network) or at the token-generation boundary? We need consistent metrics for our SLA verification.
2) Burst: we like the 30% idea. Can you confirm whether burst is capacity-based (GPU-hours) or throughput-based (requests/sec)? For our planning we prefer throughput-based burst guarantees for short events.
3) Support: we need 24/7 coverage and an on-call phone escalation path — please provide an on-call escalation matrix (names/titles okay to redact).
4) Procurement: our procurement team has two items: a) shortened auto-renew notice (we prefer 60 days) and b) a mutual NDA carveout around performance logs.

I've attached our internal question list for the SLA (FastRetail_SLA_Questions.pdf) and looped in procurement. If you can reply with concrete language, we can parallel review with legal.

Thanks — Anna
Anna Lopez
Head of AI Platforms
FastRetail
anna.lopez@fastretail.com | +1 (212) 555-0167

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 08:41:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: FastRetail SLA upgrade & capacity term transition — internal notes

Sean / Rishi — quick internal play: responses below to Anna's asks. I drafted the redline (attached) with the concessions I think we can take without exec signoff.

Summary recommendations (short):
- Latency measurement: state as 'end-to-end inference latency at Redwood edge measured at model invocation boundary (client request received to first token emitted)', with an observability hook for customer to query p50/p95/p99 per route. This matches our telemetry.
- Burst semantics: implement as throughput-based burst (requests/sec) with a 10-min sliding window; translate 30% burst into an equivalent RPS uplift on committed capacity. Ops will document the mapping.
- Support matrix: provide 24/7 phone escalation path (Tier 3 on-call + SRE rotation); for contact list provide roles not personal emails in public doc, full contact list will be available in the private SOW.
- Procurement asks: agree to 60-day renewal notice (we normally do 90) but push back on mutual NDA carveout for logs — propose a limited access model instead (aggregated metrics + redacted traces).

Attached: SLA-Amendment-Redline.docx (tracks changes), suggested customer-facing summary to include in the order form.

Action items:
- Sean: reply to Anna with redline and proposed DocuSign envelope (we can pre-fill order + SLD) — target Friday 1/22
- Rishi: confirm we can commit to p95 200ms on the target model family for the stated provisioned capacity; flag if this needs an exec kick.

-Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@fastretail.com>, FastRetail Procurement <procurement@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: FastRetail SLA upgrade & capacity term transition

Anna / procurement team — thanks for the questions. See answers inline and attached redline: SLA-Amendment-Redline.docx.

- Latency metric: confirmed — we measure end-to-end inference latency at the model invocation boundary (time from request reception at Redwood edge to first token emitted). We'll publish p50/p95/p99 via the Console and include a query template for your engineers to reproduce the calculation.

- Burst semantics: burst will be throughput-based (RPS) with a 10-minute sliding window. 30% burst means your provisioned RPS will be allowed a 30% uplift sustained in any 10-minute window for up to 6 months per renewal year (we included a 6-month higher-burst pilot to cover seasonality). Billing for burst above committed will be on usage tiers in the order form.

- Support & escalation: Premium SLA includes 24/7 phone line, 30-minute Sev-1 response, and a named Tier-3 rotation. We'll share roles and escalation matrix in the private SOW; public doc will include role titles and our escalation playbook.

- Procurement items: we're ok with 60-day renewal notice. For logs, we cannot accept a full mutual NDA carveout; propose limited-access logs for FastRetail (redacted request ids + aggregated metrics) and a secure, auditable access request process for full traces subject to escalation.

Next steps:
1) I've attached the redline to the proposed SLA amendment.
2) If that looks good procurement can sign via DocuSign (link below).

DocuSign (amendment + order form): https://www.docusign.com/en/sign?envelopeId=0a1b2c3d4e5f
Attachments: SLA-Amendment-Redline.docx, FastRetail_Renewal_MAAP_v2.pdf

Let me know if you want a short ops sync this week to walk through telemetry and the burst mapping.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
